headline: When star goalies get traded in their primes: A case study
take:
Daily Faceoff ran a case study this week on star goalies who changed teams in their primes, a list that now includes Connor Hellebuyck, who has moved to New Jersey. Daily Faceoff also posted that he lived up to expectations in his Devils debut, stopping 17 of 18 shots for a .944 save percentage.

One game proves little, but our numbers back up the early read. Goals saved above expected, which measures how many goals a goalie prevents compared with what an average goalie would allow on the same shots, has Hellebuyck at 0.71 so far this season for NJD. Last season he posted 3.43 over 57 games, so the baseline is clearly that of a goalie who beats the average. For a Devils team that needed a difference-maker in net, that is the number to track. We'd watch whether he keeps stopping more than the shot quality says he should, since that is what separates a star from a hot week. Hellebuyck was drafted 130th overall by the Jets in 2012, a reminder that goalies rarely arrive as obvious stars.
